nodes.description: No disease-specific therapy is approved and no clinical trial has been reported. In alpha2delta-4 knockout mice, subretinal AAV delivery of alpha2delta-4 to photoreceptors restored synaptic localization of Cav1.4, ELFN proteins and mGluR6, retinal function and visual acuity, and prevented rod degeneration. The benefit depended on age: rod transmission was not restored when treatment started in middle age, while cone transmission was. Both studies are preprints. An exon-skipping antisense approach was tested and found unsuitable because the skipped alpha2delta-4 proteins are nonfunctional (PMID:26218913).

nodes.description: Biallelic CACNA2D4 variants (nonsense, multi-exon deletions, a splice-altering deletion, and rare missense changes) remove or truncate the alpha2delta-4 auxiliary subunit. The recurrent p.Tyr802* nonsense variant truncates about one-third of the open reading frame and is predicted to cause nonsense-mediated decay or loss of the delta peptide that anchors the subunit at the membrane; the mouse frameshift allele sharply reduces Cacna2d4 transcript. alpha2delta-4 normally increases current through the L-type channel it partners.

The index siblings had a mild, slowly progressive cone dystrophy rather than night blindness. Other reports describe a non-progressive cone-dominant retinal dysfunction, so whether the cone disorder progresses varies between families.

nodes.description: In alpha2delta-4 knockout retina, rod bipolar, cone bipolar and horizontal cell processes extend abnormally into the outer nuclear layer, a remodeling response to the loss of normal photoreceptor synaptic contacts. Neonatal gene supplementation in mice prevents it, whereas later treatment restores synaptic proteins without reversing the sprouting. Not documented in human patients, whose retinal imaging is usually normal.

nodes.description: Mouse models lose photoreceptors slowly: the spontaneous mutant loses rods while cones are spared until about 6 weeks, the knockout shows slow photoreceptor degeneration, and an all-cone knockout retina loses about 10% of cones by 2 months. Human patients have mostly not shown retinal degeneration, including over 17 years of follow-up in one patient, so this node is largely a model finding (see the HUMAN_MODEL_MISMATCH discussion). Single reports of retinitis pigmentosa with CACNA2D4 variants are the only possible human counterpart.

nodes.description: Without alpha2delta-4, fewer Cav1.4 channels reach and remain at the photoreceptor presynaptic terminal and the remaining channels conduct less current. Zebrafish cacna2d4b knockout reduces expression of the Cav1.4 pore subunit, indicating that this trafficking role is conserved.

nodes.description: Reduced calcium entry at photoreceptor ribbon synapses, together with failed rod synapse assembly, reduces glutamatergic transmission from photoreceptors to ON- and OFF-bipolar cells. This is the convergent synaptic endpoint of the disease, read out clinically as a reduced b-wave relative to the a-wave and as abnormal light-adapted responses on the full-field ERG. In humans the cone pathway is most affected; in the mouse rod transmission is abolished as well. Conformance to the synaptic vesicle cycle module is at its endpoint only: the lesion is in the calcium channel that triggers release, not in a vesicle-cycle protein, and the affected synapse is the photoreceptor ribbon synapse rather than a cortical or neuromuscular one.

nodes.description: In rods of the spontaneous Cacna2d4 mutant mouse, internal calcium stores are depleted and calcium and sodium entry through non-selective cation channels is upregulated. The authors propose that store depletion, with the resulting cation overload and endoplasmic reticulum stress, drives rod death. Shown only in the mouse.

nodes.description: Retinitis pigmentosa has been reported in one Chinese proband carrying two CACNA2D4 missense variants, whose pathogenicity the authors call possible. A second report of retinitis pigmentosa involved only a heterozygous CACNA2D4 deletion together with another candidate gene and is not counted here. Evidence that CACNA2D4 causes retinitis pigmentosa is weak.
